rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis uses a Si doping to form a Si-rich interfacial phase during sintering at ~1700 °C, whereas the target uses a 30% AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder consolidated by spark plasma sintering at 1300–1600 °C. These are fundamentally different kinds of intervention (dopant vs. metallic binder).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies sintering at ~1700 °C in an inert or slightly reducing atmosphere, while the target uses SPS at 1300–1600 °C under vacuum. The service conditions in the hypothesis (oxidation at 1200–1400 °C, liquid plating-metal bath) differ from the target's molten Al at 700 °C and room-temperature wear. The broad regime of lower-temperature sintering is shared, but the specific conditions are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis mechanism relies on a Si-rich interfacial phase that lowers sintering activation energy and forms a protective silica barrier. The target mechanism involves liquid HEA binder fluidity, pore filling, and grain bonding improving densification up to 1500 °C, with binder loss causing degradation at 1600 °C. These are different classes of mechanism (silica barrier vs. liquid-phase sintering and binder loss).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance and comparable strength relative to high-temperature ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens. The target predicts and measures the best density, hardness, fracture toughness, molten-Al corrosion resistance, and wear resistance at 1500 °C among the tested SPS temperatures. The properties overlap partially (corrosion resistance), but the specific comparisons and measured properties differ substantially.
